$comment: The badge kit of one repository (FS04-031, WEB-084; ops decision D115, slices P13b and P16a, and ops decisions D150, D151 and D154, the README card): what a repository's administrator pastes into a README, and the addresses of the repository's project cards. Two implementations compose it from the same inputs, the dashboard's api in C# and the website's registry page in JavaScript, and each is held to this file member for member and character for character, so a snippet copied from the dashboard and one copied from the repository's public page are the same text.

`input` is the repository's GitHub node id, its `owner/name`, the origin the edge answers on and the public site's origin. `kit` is the answer. `endpoint`, `markdown` and `html` are the shields.io endpoint (`/badge/{nodeId}.json`) and its two snippets. `page` is the registry page every snippet links to. `flat` and `card` are the repository's own badges (openapi/edge-public.v1.yaml `getRepositoryBadge`): the flat badge, and the 420×88 card in a light and a dark version, whose HTML is one `<picture>` that shows the dark version under `prefers-color-scheme: dark`; Markdown cannot switch, so the card's Markdown shows the light one. `projectCard` (1200×630) and `socialPreview` (1280×640, for GitHub's repository social preview) are the project cards (`getRepositoryCard`).

`readme` is the README card, `getRepositoryBadge`'s twelve card names: the two cards the adoption pull request writes into a README, `top` (440×84, for the top of a README) and `showcase` (the full card, for its License section). Each names its three icons, `mark` (Purpose Source's mark, the default), `picture` (the repository owner's GitHub picture) and `noicon`, each with its light `url` and its `darkUrl`. Its `section` is the marked part the adoption tool writes for that form, with Purpose Source's mark and the contributors' line, byte for byte, its fingerprint included, so a part pasted by hand is one the tool knows as its own and never adds a second beside. The README card needs the repository's `owner/name`, which the card's alt text names, and each implementation offers it only where the deployment's edge serves the cards.
Every snippet names the canonical hosts verbatim (CERT-027). A snippet changes here first, and then in both implementations in the same release.
